boundaries: The subgroup enumeration is complete only inside one four-line spread-pair stabilizer H isomorphic to S4 x D8, not across all subgroups of PGSp(4,3).
The rank-three spread association scheme and rook-double identification are q=3 finite theorems; no all-q generalization is asserted.
Quadratic representation multiplicities establish allowed equivariant channels, not nonzero physical coupling constants.
Hardware items are architectures and prototypes to build, not demonstrated devices or fundamental-particle identifications.
theorems: The size-540 and size-1620 order-four classes are decoration bundles of degrees two and six over the 270 four-line spread pairs: coherent linewise quarter-turns and cyclic orders of the four common lines.

Complete subgroup enumeration inside H=S4 x D8 finds 33 H-conjugacy classes that construct 60-frame exact covers from whole frame orbits; every successful subgroup has order 2, 4, or 8, with a literal D8 witness using twelve orbits.
The 36 spreads form a rank-three association scheme. The four-line relation is SRG(36,15,6,6), satisfies A^2=9I+6J, and forces every other spread pair to meet in exactly one line.

The 360 one-line spread-pair orbit does not fiber over the 45 octets. Its intrinsic local geometry is the bipartite double cover of the 3x3 rook graph, whose automorphism group has order 144, exactly the pair stabilizer.

Degrees 240 and 540 are unsafe for count-only G-set identification. The 90-sector phase is linearly confined but quadratically connected, motivating separated geometric mixing, orbit scheduling, quadratic readout, and stabilizer-aware interfaces.
